paragraphs.p1: In this report, MyFace has approached the commissioned facial analysis from a cephalometric point of view, taking soft tissue measurements and comparing them with established scientific reference ranges for facial harmony and proportion.
paragraphs.p2: This approach makes the report's findings less subjective where recommendations may vary from person to person.

paragraphs.p1: This report is provided for general informational and educational purposes only. It discusses topics related to facial aesthetics, orthodontics, and other health related subjects. It is not intended to constitute, and should not be relied upon as, medical, clinical, or professional advice, diagnosis, or treatment of any kind.
paragraphs.p2: The information provided by MyFace, MyFace Inc., and their affiliates is not a substitute for consultation with a qualified medical or healthcare professional. Readers should always seek the advice of an appropriately licensed professional regarding any medical condition, treatment, or decision.
paragraphs.p3: MyFace, MyFace Inc., and their affiliates make no representations or warranties, express or implied, regarding the accuracy, reliability, timeliness, or completeness of the information contained in this report, and expressly disclaim any liability arising from reliance on its contents. Any actions taken based on this report are done solely at the reader's own risk.
paragraphs.p4: The purpose of this report is solely to help the reader understand their facial features and how certain treatments or recommendations could potentially impact appearance. Any reference to treatments, procedures, or outcomes is provided for informational context only. The final decision on whether any treatment or intervention is appropriate must be made by a qualified medical or healthcare professional.

privacy.p1: The contents of this report have been produced for the intended client and all supplied original content by the client including but not limited to images and videos are stored offline for 30 days in the event of revisions or corrections to the supplied report.
privacy.p2: The MyFace brand does not use supplied client material for any purpose other than for the intended report the client has provided consent for. By supplying visual content (images, videos) to MyFace, it is implicitly assumed that the client provides consent for MyFace to use it in the client's report.
privacy.p3: This produced report is intended for the client only and will not be distributed to anyone other than the client. MyFace reserves the right to store the report offline for up to 1 year for reference purposes.
privacy.p4: Client-supplied images that have been modified by MyFace will be stored as a whole within the report.
privacy.p5: The MyFace brand does use cookies on the myface.club website to help aid navigation, analytics and browsing metadata. This process does track browser usage throughout the site.

protocolModel.limitations: Limitations apply: neutral head position, lighting, camera quality, and the absence of radiographic imaging may influence measurements. This report is not a medical diagnosis. Recommendations throughout should be taken as empirical guidelines grounded in the subject's facial measurements.

understandingResults.p1: These recommendations focus on key markers of facial health and harmony. The goal is not to change what makes the subject unique, but to understand what works best with the subject's existing features.
understandingResults.p2: MyFace does not rate attractiveness. The assessment highlights what works best for the subject's features using objective cephalometric measurements rather than a single universal standard.
understandingResults.p3: The protocol includes a mix of foundational and more advanced recommendations. Fundamentals such as SPF, sleep, and hydration support the effectiveness of more targeted guidance.
understandingResults.p4: All recommendations are for informational and aesthetic purposes only. Any in-clinic treatment or prescription product should be discussed with a qualified medical professional.

protocolModel.closingPending: Closing recommendations for this protocol are being prepared from the subject's stored measurements. Reopen the protocol after generation completes, or contact support if this message persists.
protocolModel.closingHarmony: The assessment shows overall facial harmony described as average from facial measurements under the lighting and pose of this session, not a medical diagnosis.
protocolModel.closingPlan30: A practical 30-day plan is: daily broad-spectrum SPF 50 outdoors; gentle cleansing morning and night; adequate sleep and hydration; and feature-specific grooming noted on each protocol page. Avoid aggressive actives until tolerance is clear.
protocolModel.closingRepeat: Repeat analysis under consistent lighting, a neutral expression, and the same camera distance to compare progress. Discuss persistent or progressive concerns with a qualified clinician; this report does not replace clinical examination.
protocolModel.closingDisclaimer: This protocol is informational guidance from the facial measurements, not medical diagnosis or treatment.

protocolModel.protocolLeadAfter: The analysis is designed to be objective. Instead of comparing the subject to a universal ideal, it highlights strengths and areas for improvement, recognizing that each person's features offer unique possibilities.

featureReport.subtitle: Facial landmark balance from your photos

brow.subtitle: Eyebrows are one of the most important facial features and play a key role in expressing emotion.

peak.body: Vertical distance from the brow peak to the top of the eye — measures how high the brow sits above the eye.

elevation.body: Brow-to-eye vertical gap divided by inter-pupillary distance. Higher = brow sits further above the eye.

apex.body: Angle at the brow peak between inner and outer brow vectors. Smaller angle = sharper, more defined arch.

eye.subtitle: The eyes are a focal point of facial harmony and play a key role in expressing emotion.

curvature.body: Sagitta/chord ratio measuring how curved the lower eyelid contour appears. Higher value = more rounded contour.

ear.body: EAR = vertical opening / horizontal width. Higher = more open, almond-shaped eye.

spacing.body: Interpupillary distance divided by facial width. Closer to 0.5 = eyes spaced at half the face width (classic aesthetic ideal).

jaw.subtitle: The jawline frames the lower face and contributes to overall harmony.

rise.body: Vertical drop from the gonion (jaw angle) to the menton (chin tip). Higher = more defined, angular jawline.

width.body: Bi-gonial width — the horizontal distance between both jaw angle landmarks.

angle.body: Average jaw inclination angle. Smaller = sharper V/U shape. Larger = more square jaw.

chin.subtitle: Chin width, projection, and depth balance the lower face and support overall harmony.

width.body: Horizontal distance between lateral chin points. Typical range 37–47 mm.

height.body: Distance from the lower lip base to the chin tip. Typical range 12–22 mm.

dev.body: How far the chin tip deviates from the nasion–nose-tip vertical axis. Ideal ≈ 0 mm.

smile.subtitle: Mouth width and smile-arc curvature shape expression and lower-face harmony.

upper.body: Sagitta / chord ratio of the upper smile arc. Higher = more upturned upper lip smile curve.

lower.body: Sagitta / chord ratio for the lower smile arc (lower lip). Indicates how curved the lower smile appears.

width.body: Mouth corner-to-corner width at rest. Typical range 40–60 mm.

neck.subtitle: Neck width and its proportion to the jaw support lower-face framing and overall harmony.

width.body: Horizontal span of the neck region from the segmentation mask. Typical range 80–100 mm.

ratio.body: Ratio of neck width to jaw width. Closer to 0.7–0.8 is typically considered proportionate.

nose.subtitle: The nose is a central pillar of facial aesthetics and plays a key role in overall harmony.

aspect.body: Width divided by height. <0.6 = narrow, 0.6–0.85 = average, >0.85 = wide.

width.body: Distance between the alae (outer nostrils) in millimetres. Reference IPD = 63.5 mm.

nasoCanthal.body: Alar width / inter-canthal distance. Ideal ≈ 1.0 (nose width = inner eye distance).

lips.subtitle: The lips frame expression and proportion in the lower face and contribute to overall harmony.

mouthWidth.body: Horizontal distance between the mouth corners. Typical range 40–60 mm.

cupid.body: Angle at the Cupid's bow dip. Lower = more peaked/defined upper lip arch.

philtrum.body: Distance from subnasale (base of nose) to the Cupid's bow dip. Typical range 10–20 mm.

hair.subtitle: Hairline and forehead geometry frame the upper face and contribute to overall harmony.

foreheadWidth.body: Distance between temple landmarks. Broader temples give more flexibility in choosing hairstyles.

foreheadHeight.body: Vertical distance from the mesh forehead top to the glabella. Typical range 50–75 mm.

temple.body: Angle from vertical between temple and zygion landmarks. Reflects how much the temples flare outward.

cheek.subtitle: Cheekbones frame midface width and height and contribute to overall harmony.

malar.body: Facial width / face height. Higher = broader, more angular face shape.

position.body: Vertical position of the cheekbone apex as a fraction of face height. Lower value = higher set cheekbones.

facialWidth.body: Bizygomatic width — distance between the outermost cheekbone points.

skin.subtitle: Skin tone, texture and uniformity are analysed using LAB color science and Laplacian frequency analysis.

roughness.body: Your skin's roughness is estimated from Laplacian variance on skin pixels. Higher RIN means more fine textural grain at close range.

homogeneity.body: Colour homogeneity measured from standard deviation across LAB channels. Lower RIN = more even tone.

oiliness.body: Luminance skewness detects specular highlights from sebum. Positive skew → shiny/oily; negative → matte/dry.

underEye.body: Compares under-eye brightness against average face luminance. A lower ratio indicates dark circles.

angular_fringe.title: Angular Fringe
angular_fringe.explanation: An angular fringe creates stronger forehead lines while keeping the sides clean for a modern, intentional look.

balanced_side_part.title: Balanced Side Part
balanced_side_part.explanation: A balanced side part with controlled mid-length volume suits a polished neutral look.

buzz_crew_cut.title: Buzz/Crew Cut
buzz_crew_cut.explanation: A short buzz or crew cut with tight edges is low-maintenance and keeps facial features clearly visible.

classic_taper_side_part.explanation: A classic taper with a side part keeps framing tidy and calms facial proportions.

curtain_fringe_side_volume.explanation: A curtain fringe with side volume adds width while keeping the top controlled.
